references.text: A parallel command to make tassels (tzitzit) on the four corners of a garment.
The use of blue (tekhelet) dye in priestly garments, the same color that was to be used in the tassels.
A blue cord used to attach the gold plate on the turban, the same blue color (tekhelet) as in the tassels.
Reference to the corner (kanaf) of a garment, the same word used for the corners where the tassels were to be attached.
The continuation of the command explaining the purpose of the tassels: to remember the Lord's commands.
The woman with bleeding touched the edge (κράσπεδον) of Jesus' garment, referring to the tzitzit tassels.
People asked to touch the edge (κράσπεδον) of Jesus' garment for healing.
Jesus criticizes the Pharisees for making their tassels (κράσπεδα) large to be seen by others.
The woman touched the edge (κράσπεδον) of Jesus' garment, parallel to the account in Matthew.
